cards.body:
## Summary
The slip's first sentence - what will happen and whether it can be taken back - is guessed from the English verb in the tool's name, while the gate classifies the same tool from the flags the app declared. Six gated tools in the shipped apps and connectors (mark_paid, decide_stage, merge_contacts, tidycrm undo, Notion append_to_page and create_page) are irreversible or leave the boundary, yet their card says only 'X is changed in <app>.' Conversely any reversible tool whose verb is archive/close/cancel is told it 'cannot be undone'. Make the declaration the authority and the verb only the wording.

## Description
`describeDecision` takes an optional `flags: {reversible: boolean|null, side_effects: string}`. Risk is derived: external -> outbound, reversible false -> destructive, reversible true -> change, none -> read. When flags are missing or reversible is null the card takes the severe bucket and says so ('The app did not declare whether this can be undone.'), per hitl-approval/fail-loud-classification-default: an unreadable classification must not share a spelling with a mild one. `DecisionWords` gains `declared: boolean`. The OUTBOUND/DESTRUCTIVE verb sets survive only to choose sentence shape ('will receive' versus 'reaches outside'), never the promise. `toolRows` keeps `flagsOf`'s answer on the row (two optional fields on ToolRow); `cardView` looks the card's flags up in `tools` (page tools) or the connectors mirror (connector tools) and passes them through. The class shown and sent to the gate is untouched: tightening (first sight, pinned, drifted contract) still makes a row GATED, and the words still read what the app declared.

## Flow
- Page registers tools -> toolRows rows carry class + reversible + side_effects
- Card arrives -> cardView finds the tool's flags (page row or connector mirror)
- describeDecision derives risk and the take-back sentence from the flags; undeclared -> severe + marked
- Slip front shows that sentence; nothing about the gate changes

## Expected impact
The one sentence a person signs against stops contradicting the contract the gate enforces. Six real tools today understate their consequence; after, a card can only overstate when the app declined to declare, and then it says that is why. Closes the whole class 'card promise drifts from manifest' rather than patching verb lists.

## Evaluation
Claim: the card's take-back promise equals the tool's declared flags for every declared tool, and undeclared reads severe and marked.
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (cases 0-3, 6, 7); guards 4-5 pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases in translate.test.ts, model.test.ts, tools.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.body:
## Summary
When a decision rises, the person signs against one sentence and three facts. Whatever the turn already read about the card's target - a dispute note on the invoice, how many days overdue it is, when she read it - stays one level down in a step's table that the slip never shows. A person can approve a chase of a disputed invoice without the window ever putting the dispute in front of them, though the window holds it.

## Description
`buildContext` records, per id, the clock and tool of the step that last read it (`TurnContext.seen`). `describeDecision` adds `standing: {notes, facts, readAt, readBy} | null` for the card's target: notes are the record's NOTE_KEY fields, facts its AGE_KEY fields formatted as the table formats them, readAt/readBy the provenance in plain words. It is generic over the existing vocabulary, so no tool gets per-tool copy. The slip's front, the rail's Gate and each sheet row show the notes as a `role=note` notice above the sign row, and one quiet line 'As she read it at 09:41: Read the inbox in Ledgerbox' so the person knows how old the knowledge is (hitl-approval/decision-records: what the decider saw is part of the decision; oracle-before-gate: give the reviewer the thing to check against). No message on the rail changes.

## Flow
- Turn reads records -> buildContext keeps each id's record plus when and by which step
- A card arrives about one of those ids -> describeDecision attaches its standing
- Slip / Gate / sheet row render the note notice and the as-of line; absent target -> nothing extra

## Expected impact
The person stops signing blind to facts the window already has: a dispute, a warning, an age, and how stale that reading is - on the surface where they press A, not two clicks away.

## Evaluation
Claim: a card about a record the turn read surfaces that record's notes, age and provenance on every form of the card.
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard acceptance cases pass; guard 7 passes
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases in translate.test.ts, slip.test.tsx, ledger.test.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
